tally.headline: 0 of 2 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 8.3 points toward Sacramento State of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured (stale 93h) · FanDuel. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 52.9 sat 4.4 points above the captured total of 48.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: None of the mechanism EdgeDesk named before kickoff could be graded against the statistics published for this game. The scoreboard is not evidence about a mechanism nobody could observe.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 3-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Massachusetts Minutemen won the turnover battle by 3. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

variance_markers.label: A 29-point margin
variance_markers.text: Once a game is this far apart both teams stop playing the game they were rated on — the leader runs clock, the trailer throws — so late-game rates describe the situation rather than either team.

variance_markers.label: 1 non-offensive or return score
variance_markers.text: Points that arrived without an offensive drive. They count the same on the scoreboard and belong to a different distribution from the one the model prices.

verdict.line: The number did not land, in a game the statistics cannot grade the reasoning on. It goes in the record and teaches little.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk makes it Sacramento State -3.8 where the market has Sacramento State +4.5 at captured (stale 104h) · FanDuel — a 8.3 points disagreement. EdgeDesk prices this game at Sacramento State -3.8 with a fair total of 51.6, which makes Sacramento State the better team here by that margin on this field.
lessons.actual_result: Sacramento State Hornets lost by 29. Sacramento State Hornets lost by 29 where EdgeDesk projected a 3.8-point edge.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Sacramento State as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 12.1 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 7 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: The model published an outcome range of -19.2 → +24.8 (Sacramento State).
lessons.actual_result: The game finished outside it, at a margin of 29.
lessons.lesson: The published range is meant to contain eight results in ten. A miss is expected roughly twice in ten games and is only a problem in aggregate — which is exactly what this store exists to measure.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Count range misses across the season. A rate materially above 20% means the model’s stated uncertainty is too narrow.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Sacramento State -3.8 where the market has Sacramento State +4.5 at captured (stale 104h) · FanDuel — a 8.3 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Sacramento State Hornets lost by 29. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
